summary:
## Verdict

**Critical CORS misconfiguration** — this change disables origin allowlisting and reflects arbitrary `Origin` values while always sending `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`.

## Why this is blocking

The previous code only echoed an origin when it was in a fixed allowlist (`https://app.example.com`). The new code returns ACAO for **any** caller-supplied origin (or `*` when `origin` is null), still with credentials enabled.

Failure mode: any malicious site can trigger a credentialed cross-origin request (cookies / client certs / Authorization in some setups) and **read the response**, because the browser will treat that site as an allowed origin. That is a direct break of the prior same-origin trust boundary.

Secondary issue: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is invalid per the Fetch/CORS spec; browsers reject it. So the `origin ?? "*"` branch does not actually help null-Origin native clients either.

Mobile webviews with varying origins need an explicit allowlist (or a non-cookie auth model), not open reflection.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The change removed the origin allowlist and now always sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to the request origin (or *) together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, which enables credentialed cross-origin reads and is invalid for the * case.
